rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qist is justice when directed toward truth and injustice when directed toward falsehood.
rows.anchor: أصل القسط العدل فإذا كان إلى جهة الحق فهو عدل ومنه قوله إن الله يحب المقسطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikhlas is removing foreign admixture; sincerity to God means directing worship exclusively to Him.
rows.anchor: وأصل الإخلاص إخراج كل شائب من الجنس ومنه إخلاص الدين لله وهو توجيه العبادة إليه خالصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning is doing something for the first time and return is doing it a second time; a verb can also name an act's first phase.
rows.anchor: والبداء فعل الشيء أول مرة والعود فعله ثاني مرة وقد يكون فعل أول خصلة منه بدء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fariq is a group separated from another group.
rows.anchor: والفريق جماعة انفصلت من جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittikhadh derives from taking and means preparing something for a particular purpose.
rows.anchor: والاتخاذ افتعال من الأخذ بمعنى إعداد الشيء لأمر من الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hisab is a strong conjecture that still allows the imagined possibility to be otherwise; possibility separates it from knowledge, while strength separates it from imitation and guesswork.
rows.anchor: والحسبان بمعنى الظن وهو ما قوي عند الظان كون المظنون كل ما ظنه مع تجويزه

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: He coordinates “establish your faces” with the preceding prohibition against Satan, with an implied “beware Satan.”
rows.anchor: وأقيموا عطف على ما تقدم من قوله لا يفتننكم الشيطان فتقديره احذروا الشيطان وأقيموا وجوهكم عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative parsing supplies “and say” after “my Lord commanded justice”: “My Lord commanded justice, and say: establish your faces.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن تقديره أمر ربي بالقسط وقل أقيموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After clarifying that God does not command indecency, the passage identifies what He commands: qist, a comprehensive name for all good things.
rows.anchor: لما بين سبحانه أنه لا يأمر بالفحشاء وهو اسم جامع للقبائح والسيئات عقبه ببيان ما يأمر به من القسط

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: They explain qist as justice and uprightness.
rows.anchor: أي بالعدل والاستقامة عن مجاهد والسدي وأكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains qist as monotheism.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالتوحيد عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses qist as the declaration “there is no god but God.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: بلا إله إلا الله عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim interprets qist as all acts of obedience and devotion.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بجميع الطاعات والقرب عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: One reading is to face the qibla correctly at every mosque during prayer.
rows.anchor: أن معناه توجهوا إلى قبلة كل مسجد في الصلاة على استقامة عن مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد

rows.speaker: الجبائي وغيره
rows.claim: Another reading directs worshippers toward the Kaaba, the direction God commanded; “mosque” means the times of prostration, or prayer times.
rows.anchor: أقيموا وجوهكم إلى الجهة التي أمركم الله بالتوجه إليها في صلاتكم وهي الكعبة والمراد بالمسجد أوقات السجود

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: If someone reaches a mosque at prayer time, they should pray there instead of waiting to return to their own mosque; here “mosque” is the place of prostration. Al-Maghribi prefers this view.
rows.anchor: عن الفراء وهو اختيار المغربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth interpretation commands attending the mosque for each prayer and praying in congregation; most scholars consider this recommended, while a minority consider it obligatory.
rows.anchor: قصدوا المسجد في وقت كل صلاة أمر بالجماعة لهذا ندبا عند الأكثرين وحتما عند الأقلين

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabi interprets the command as devoting oneself to God in obedience without associating an idol or anything else with Him.
rows.anchor: أخلصوا وجوهكم لله تعالى في الطاعة فلا تشركوا به وثنا ولا غيره عن الربيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to supplicate humbly to God after making religion sincere to Him.
rows.anchor: وهذا أمر بالدعاء والتضرع إليه سبحانه على وجه الإخلاص أي أرغبوا إليه في الدعاء بعد إخلاصكم له الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation takes “invoke Him” to mean worship Him with religion made sincere to Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه واعبدوه مخلصين له الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One connection is that sincere prayer matters because people will be resurrected and recompensed; the first creation should convince them of the second, even if resurrection seems implausible.
rows.anchor: وادعوه مخلصين فإنكم مبعوثون ومجازون وإن بعد ذلك في عقولكم فاعتبروا بالابتداء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj connects the phrase with the preceding promise that people live, die, and emerge from the earth: resurrection is no harder than their initial creation, an argument against those denying resurrection.
rows.anchor: أنه يتصل بقوله فيها تحيون وفيها تموتون ومنها تخرجون فقال كما بدأكم تعودون أي فليس بعثكم بأشد

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim reads this as a new statement that God will recreate people after death and requite them.
rows.anchor: أنه كلام مستأنف أي يعيدكم بعد الموت فيجازيكم عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says people began from earth and return to it, citing “From it We created you and into it We return you.”
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: بدأكم من التراب وإليه تعودون كما قال منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation compares resurrection with the first creation when people possessed nothing: they will likewise possess nothing when raised.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه كما بدأكم لا تملكون شيئا كذلك تبعثون يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Jabir say people are raised in the state in which they died: believers in faith and disbelievers in disbelief.
rows.anchor: المؤمن على إيمانه والكافر على كفره عن ابن عباس وجابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided group may be those God judged guided because they accepted guidance, those enabled by a grace through which they became guided, or those guided to the path of reward.
rows.anchor: أي حكم لهم بالاهتداء بقبولهم للهدى أو لطف لهم بما اهتدوا عنده أو هداهم إلى طريق الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other group's error was decreed because they rejected guidance, because they lacked a grace that would open their hearts, or because their disbelief merited punishment and destruction.
rows.anchor: إذ لم يقبلوا الهدى أو حق عليهم الخذلان لأنه لم يكن لهم لطف ينشرح له صدورهم أو حق عليهم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment-and-destruction reading is supported by the following explanation that they took devils as patrons after resurrection; God recompensed their disobedience and following Satan rather than initiating punishment against them.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد هذا القول الأخير أنه سبحانه ذكر الهدى والضلال بعد العود والبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They made devils their patrons by obeying what the devils called them to.
rows.anchor: وإنما اتخذوهم أولياء بطاعتهم لهم فيما دعوهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghaniya means to dwell or remain in a place, as though one had no need of another place; maghani means dwellings. Hatim al-Ta'i's poem illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: غني بالمكان يغني غنا وغنيانا أقام به كأنه استغنى بذلك المكان عن غيره والمغاني المنازل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asa means intense grief; the source also cites an Arabic poetic line using the word.
rows.anchor: والأسى شدة الحزن يقول أسي يأسي أسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You will be losers” answers the oath and serves as the answer to the conditional beginning with la-in; idha is parenthetical here and the clause depends on what precedes it.
rows.anchor: إنكم إذا لخاسرون جواب القسم وقد سد مسد جواب الشرط من قوله لئن وإذا ها هنا ملغاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first “those who denied Shuayb” is nominative as subject, with “as though they had never lived there” as its predicate; repeating the phrase instead of using a pronoun intensifies the charge.
rows.anchor: الذين كذبوا سيما الأول في موضع رفع بالابتداء وخبره كأن لم يغنوا فيها وإنما أعيد مرة ثانية من غير كناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hum is a separating pronoun that emphasizes the meaning; it is needed for emphasis even though a pronoun is not ordinarily modified, and the definite predicate still functions as a predicate.
rows.anchor: وهم في قوله هم الخاسرين فصل وإنما دخل الفصل مع أن المضمر لا يوصف لأنه يحتاج فيه إلى التوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelieving leaders warned Shuayb's people that following his commands and prohibitions and abandoning their own religion would make them losers; following means the second party seeks to match the first party's call.
rows.anchor: الاتباع هو طلب الثاني موافقة الأول فيما دعا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning uses loss of capital as its image: they would be like people who had lost their principal wealth.
rows.anchor: والخسران ذهاب رأس المال فكأنهم قالوا إن اتبعتموه كنتم بمنزلة من ذهب رأس ماله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “losers” as people who have been duped.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خاسرون مغبونون عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is that they would perish.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هالكون

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the affliction as an earthquake that seized Shuayb's people.
rows.anchor: فأخذ قوم شعيب الزلزلة عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره من المفسرين
rows.claim: In the Day of the Canopy account, scorching heat drove them indoors without relief; a cool, fragrant cloud drew them outside, where it burned them as the earth shook, leaving them like fried locusts and then ashes.
rows.anchor: وهو عذاب يوم الظلة عن ابن عباس وغيره من المفسرين

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله ع
rows.claim: Abu Abdillah reports that God sent one cry against them and they died.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بعث الله عليهم صيحة واحدة فماتوا عن أبي عبد الله ع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative account distinguishes two peoples of Shuayb: one was destroyed by the quake and another was the people of the Canopy.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه كان لشعيب قومان قوم أهلكوا بالرجفة وقوم هم أصحاب الظلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were found dead, lying face down in their dwellings.
rows.anchor: أي ميتين ملقين على وجوههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction made it seem that they had never existed there.
rows.anchor: أي كأنهم لم يقيموا بها قط لأن المهلك يصير كأن لم يكن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses it as though they had not lived there in ease and self-sufficiency.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كأن لم يغنوا فيها كأن لم يعيشوا فيها مستغنين عن قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses it as though they had not inhabited the place.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كأن لم يعمروا فيها عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated phrase “those who denied Shuayb” intensifies the condemnation and underscores that they, rather than the believers, were the losers.
rows.anchor: مر معناه بين سبحانه أنهم الخاسرون دون من آمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb turned away when he saw punishment approaching, having despaired of them.
rows.anchor: شعيب أي أعرض عنهم لما رأى إقبال العذاب عليهم إعراض الآيس منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb says he delivered what his Lord commanded and counseled them sincerely, but they did not believe or accept it; their calamity resulted from their own wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: فلم تقبلوا ومعناه أن ما نزل بكم من البلاء وإن كان عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “how could I grieve?” intends a negative answer and also conveys censure: mourning for deserving disbelievers makes no sense.
rows.anchor: وإن كان على لفظ الاستفهام فالمراد به النفي لأن جوابه في هذا الموضوع لا يصح إلا بالنفي وإنما يدخله معنى الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabrisi cites the poetic question “Would he be stirred to song, though a decrepit old man?” as an illustration of the rhetorical question about grief.
rows.anchor: أطربا وأنت قنسري وهذا تسل من شعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb takes consolation in recalling his sincere advice and delivery of God's message; their stubborn disbelief makes grief over them unwarranted.
rows.anchor: وهذا تسل من شعيب بما يذكر من حاله معهم في مناصحته لهم

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhi infers that Muslims should not pray for good for unbelievers or grieve the destruction of unbelievers and wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: قال البلخي: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه لا يجوز للمسلم أن يدعو للكافر بالخير وأنه لا يجوز الحزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise is to send against the Jews, through Judgment Day, a people who inflict severe punishment by killing them and taking jizya.
rows.anchor: أي من يذيقهم ويوليهم شدة العذاب بالقتل وأخذ الجزية منهم

rows.speaker: جميع المفسرين
rows.claim: All commentators identify the people sent against them with Muhammad's community; the same interpretation is transmitted from Imam al-Baqir.
rows.anchor: والمعني به أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عند جميع المفسرين وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر ع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He infers that the Jews will have neither a state nor political might until Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن اليهود لا تكون لهم دولة إلى يوم القيامة ولا عز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿth here means command, release, or assistance; another gloss is leaving them free to sin, as in the verse about devils urging disbelievers on.
rows.anchor: وأما معنى البعث ها هنا فهو الأمر والإطلاق والمعونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description is straightforward; punishment may be called swift although deferred until Judgment because everything that is coming is near.
rows.anchor: ظاهر المعنى وإنما قال سريع العقاب وإن كان العقاب مؤخرا إلى يوم القيامة لأن كل آت فهو قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God swiftly punishes in this world whoever He wills to punish.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه سريع العقاب لمن شاء أن يعاقبه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duna dhalika is grammatically nominative as a subject but appears accusative because of its adverbial force; another analysis supplies an omitted “group” and treats the phrase as its adjective.
rows.anchor: ومنهم دون ذلك دون في موضع الرفع بالابتداء ولكنه جاء منصوبا لتمكنه في الظرفية

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan compares the adverbial accusative construction with “Your ties have been cut off” and “on the Day of Resurrection He will distinguish between you.”
rows.anchor: على قول أبي الحسن لقد تقطع بينكم وهو في موضع الرفع فجاء منصوبا لهذا المعنى وكذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, an implied noun “group” is omitted: “among them is a group below that,” with the adjective standing in its place.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت كان التقدير ومنهم جماعة دون ذلك فحذف الموصوف وقامت صفته مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾadhdhana may mean that God announced and informed; another gloss is that He swore an oath heard by the ear, and Ibn Abbas says it means He said it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه تألى ربك أي أقسم القسم الذي يسمع بالأذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's release of people against them may mean leaving them free to sin, as in the verse that says He sent devils against disbelievers to urge them on.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه التخلية وإن وقع على وجه المعصية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: The scattered groups are the Jews, dispersed among different lands and divided into varied communities.
rows.anchor: وفرقناهم في البلاد فرقا مختلفة وجماعات شتى يعني اليهود عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God divided their inclinations, causing them to disperse; this weakened their mutual support and humiliated them like the taking of jizya.
rows.anchor: بأن فرق دواعيهم حتى افترقوا في البلاد وتفرقهم ذل لهم بمنزلة أخذ الجزية لأنهم لا يتعاونون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God divided them for their religious welfare, so one group became righteous while another disobeyed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه فرقهم لما علم سبحانه من الصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous among the Israelites are those who believe in God and His messengers and obey Him.
rows.anchor: أي من هؤلاء الصالحون يعني من بني إسرائيل وهم الذين يؤمنون بالله ورسله ويطيعونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those below the righteous in rank obeyed some commands, disobeyed others, and committed some sins; this describes their condition before their later apostasy, before Jesus was sent.
rows.anchor: دون الصالح في الدرجة والمنزلة وهم الذين امتثلوا بعض الأوامر دون بعض وعملوا بعض المعاصي

rows.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes the righteous as believers in Muhammad and Jesus, and the others as disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه منهم المؤمنون بمحمد وعيسى ع ومنهم الكافرون عن عطاء ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tests were prosperity, worldly ease, abundance, and comfort, as well as hardship and calamities affecting lives and property; blessings prompt people to seek their continuance from God, while afflictions prompt them to ask relief.
rows.anchor: اختبرناهم بالرخاء في العيش والخفض في الدنيا والدعة والسعة في الرزق وبالشدائد في العيش والمصائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tests are meant to bring them back to God, obedience, and compliance with His command.
rows.anchor: أي لكي يرجعوا إلى الله تعالى وينيبوا إلى طاعته وامتثال أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although they may not have previously followed the command, “return” can mean to turn toward something; it resembles telling someone in danger to return to the straight path, or it can mean returning to their original innate disposition.
rows.anchor: فالقول فيه أن الذاهب عن الشيء قد يقال له أرجع إليه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar alone reads the verb with a damma on ṭāʾ here and in al-Qasas and al-Dukhan; the others use kasra.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وحده يبطشون ههنا وفي القصص والدخان بضم الطاء والباقون بكسرها

rows.speaker: هشام ويعقوب وأبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وإسماعيل
rows.claim: Hisham and Yaqub retain the yāʾ of kaydūnī in pause and connection; Abu Jaʿfar, Abu ʿAmr, and Ismaʿil agree in connection only, while the rest omit it in both.
rows.anchor: قرأ هشام ويعقوب كيدوني بياء في الوقف والوصل ووافقهما أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وإسماعيل في الوصل

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub reads tanẓirūnī with the yāʾ in both pause and connection.
rows.anchor: وقرأ تنظروني بالياء في الحالين يعقوب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Both yabṭishu and yabṭushu are Arabic forms, though the kasra form is more eloquent.
rows.anchor: بطش يبطش ويبطش والكسر أفصح وقال أبو علي

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Clause endings work like poetic rhyme because both mark the end; rhyme may require dropping a final yāʾ, as illustrated by al-Aʿsha and another verse of poetry.
rows.anchor: الفواصل من الكلام التام تجري مجرى القوافي لاجتماعهما في أن الفاصلة آخر الآية كما أن القافية آخر البيت

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the idols are created beings like their worshippers.
rows.anchor: أي مخلوقة أمثالكم عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets them as owned beings like their worshippers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مملوكون أمثالكم عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says they resemble people in being subjected and subdued under God's command; they cannot resist what God wills, so they are servants in the sense of being humbled.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمثالكم في التسخير أي أنهم مسخرون مذللون لأمر الله عن الأخفش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of servitude is subduing; the idols' inability to resist God's will makes them servants in the sense of being subdued.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت الأصنام غير ممتنعة مما يريد الله بها كانت في معنى العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This second command to invoke them concerns asking the idols for help in urgent needs and for removal of harm.
rows.anchor: هذا الدعاء ليس الدعاء الأول والمراد به فادعوهم في مهماتكم ولكشف الأسواء عنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative lām is a challenge meant to expose and ridicule their inability, like the demand “bring your proof if you are truthful.”
rows.anchor: هذه لام الأمر على معنى التعجيز والتهجين كما قال هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the challenge as “worship them”: will they reward or requite you if you truly expect benefit, reward, intercession, or support?
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: معناه فاعبدوهم هل يثيبونكم أو يجازونكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical questions deny that idols have limbs or senses with which to walk, defend worshippers, see, or hear; people have these faculties and surpass idols.
rows.anchor: أي ليس لهم هذه الحواس ولكم هذه الحواس فأنتم أفضل منهم فلو دعوتم وعبدتم من له الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even worshipping a living being with useful faculties would merit blame, since it too is created and governed by God.
rows.anchor: للزمكم الذم واللوم بذلك لأنها مخلوقة مربوبة فكيف تعبدون من أنتم أفضل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad challenges the polytheists to gather with their supposed partners and plot without delay; his God protects him, while their idols cannot protect them.
rows.anchor: ومعناه أن معبودي ينصرني ويدفع كيد الكائدين عني ومعبودكم لا يقدر على نصركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is to remember God's blessing by reflecting on oneself; another is to remember Him inwardly through His exalted attributes and beautiful names.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد ذكره في نفسك بصفاته العليا وأسمائه الحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God in supplication with humility and fear, qualities that make prayer more likely to be answered; remembering inwardly is farther from showing off, according to al-Jubba'i.
rows.anchor: يعني بتضرع وخوف يعني في الدعاء فإن الدعاء بالتضرع والخوف من الله تعالى أقرب إلى الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raise the voice somewhat without shouting excessively, keeping a moderate level between loudness and silence.
rows.anchor: أرفعوا أصواتكم قليلا ولا تجهروا بها جهارا بليغا حتى يكون عدلا بين ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the instruction as telling the prayer leader to recite loudly enough for those behind him to hear.
rows.anchor: إنه أمر للإمام أن يرفع صوته في الصلاة بالقراءة مقدار ما يسمع من خلفه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as mornings and evenings; these periods stand for keeping remembrance continuous.
rows.anchor: أي بالغدوات والعشيات عن قتادة والمراد به دوام الذكر واتصاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation singles out these times because the heart is free from earning a livelihood and remembrance then takes firmer root.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما خص هذين الوقتين لأنهما حال فراغ القلب عن طلب المعاش فيكون الذكر فيهما ألصق بالقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition concerns neglecting the commanded supplication and remembrance.
rows.anchor: عما أمرتك به من الدعاء والذكر

rows.speaker: ابن زيد ومجاهد وابن جريج
rows.claim: The verse may instead address those told to listen quietly to the Quran, who used to raise their voices with supplication when they heard mention of Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: وكانوا إذا سمعوا القرآن رفعوا أصواتهم بالدعاء عند ذكر الجنة أو النار عن ابن زيد ومجاهد وابن جريج

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says the verse shows that people who raise their voices in supplication are mistaken and contrary to the right course.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي: وفي الآية دليل على أن الذين يرفعون أصواتهم عند الدعاء ويجهرون به مخطئن

rows.speaker: الحسن وغيره
rows.claim: Those “at your Lord” are angels; despite their exalted standing, they worship and remember God, so humans should not be arrogant about worship.
rows.anchor: وهم الملائكة عن الحسن وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “At your Lord” honors the angels through attribution to God; it does not mean spatial proximity, since God is transcendent above place.
rows.anchor: ولم يرد به قرب المكان تعالى الله عن ذلك وتقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explains the phrase as being in a place God has honored and under His sole rule, like soldiers said to be “at the prince” because they are under his authority.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه إنهم في المكان الذي شرفه الله تعالى ولا يملك عليهم الحكم إلا الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains being “at God” as being close to His grace and favor.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: من قرب من رحمة الله وفضله فهو عند الله أي هو قريب من فضله وإحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels glorify God by declaring Him free of what does not befit Him.
rows.anchor: أي ينزهونه عما لا يليق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujūd may mean humility, prayer, or prostration in prayer; al-Hasan gives the last explanation.
rows.anchor: أي يخضعون. وقيل: يصلون. وقيل: يسجدون في الصلاة عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is consensus that this is a recitation prostration and the first such sajda in the Quran; Abu Hanifa deems recitation prostration obligatory, while al-Shafi'i and the author's companions call it a confirmed sunnah.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف أن ههنا سجدة وهي أول سجدات القرآن واختلف في سجدة التلاوة هل هي واجبة فعند أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intiha is desisting from something because of a prohibition; sunna and tariqa are synonyms for a way or practice.
rows.anchor: الانتهاء الإقلاع عن الشيء لأجل النهي يقال نهاه عن كذا فانتهى والسنة والطريقة والسيرة نظائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salaf means those who came before; tawalli from religion means turning away toward its opposite, while tawalli in religion means turning toward truth and following it.
rows.anchor: والسلوف التقدم والتولي عن الدين الذهاب عنه إلى خلافه والتولي فيه هو الذهاب إلى جهة الحق ومتابعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Know that God is your protector” follows the conditional as a command functioning like a declarative answer, with the sense that knowing it is incumbent.
rows.anchor: وإن تولوا شرط وقوله فاعلموا أن الله مولاكم أمر في موضع الجواب وإنما جاز ذلك لأن فيه معنى الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands the Prophet to invite the unbelievers to repentance and faith.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر سبحانه نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بدعائهم إلى التوبة والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they repent from and desist from their polytheism, their past sins will be forgiven.
rows.anchor: أي يتوبوا عما هم عليه من الشرك ويمتنعوا منه

words: إِن يَنتَهُوا۟ يُغْفَرْ لَهُم مَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that if they stop fighting and make peace, their past punishments will be forgiven.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن ينتهوا عن المحاربة إلى الموادعة يغفر لهم ما قد سلف من المعاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they return to fighting and persist in disbelief, God's established treatment of their ancestors will apply: believers are supported and enemies humiliated, captured, and enslaved.
rows.anchor: وإن يعودوا إلى القتال وأصروا على الكفر فقد مضت سنة الله في آبائكم وعادته في نصر المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The customary outcome is attributed to those who undergo it, to messengers through whom it is carried out, and to God as its cause.
rows.anchor: وأضاف السنة إليهم لأنها كانت تجري عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan take fitna here as polytheism; the aim is to end the religious sedition that arises when an unprotected unbeliever has influence and calls people to his faith.
rows.anchor: أي شرك عن ابن عباس والحسن ومعناه حتى لا يكون كافر بغير عهد لأن الكافر إذا كان بغير عهد كان عزيزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that fighting should continue until no believer is seduced away from his religion.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حتى لا يفتن مؤمن عن دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religion will belong wholly to God when people unite around the true religion in their beliefs and practices.
rows.anchor: أي ويجتمع أهل الحق وأهل الباطل على الدين الحق فيما يعتقدونه ويعملون به

rows.speaker: زرارة وغيره عن أبي عبد الله ع
rows.claim: Zarara and others report from Abu Abdillah that this verse's fulfillment has not yet arrived; when the Qa'im rises, his contemporaries will see it fulfilled, and Muhammad's religion will reach everywhere until no polytheist remains on earth.
rows.anchor: وروى زرارة وغيره عن أبي عبد الله ع أنه قال لم يجىء تأويل هذه الآية ولو قام قائمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdn, residence, and eternity are synonymous; al-Aʿsha's poem uses ʿadana in the sense of remaining or settling.
rows.anchor: العدن والإقامة والخلود نظائر ومنه المعدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ridwan is the verbal noun of radiya, while jihad means undertaking a difficult matter and derives from jahd.
rows.anchor: والرضوان مصدر رضي يرضى رضى ورضوانا والجهاد ممارسة الأمر الشاق وأصله من الجهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the hypocrites' bad traits, the passage describes believers by their opposite qualities, linking the discussion through contrast.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر الله تعالى المنافقين ووصفهم بقبيح خصالهم اقتضت الحكمة أن يذكر المؤمنين ويصفهم بضد أوصافهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are mutual helpers and allies, each obliged to support the other; even a wife prepares her husband's journey and protects his absence, and together they stand as one against others.
rows.anchor: أي بعضهم أنصار بعض يلزم كل واحد منهم نصرة صاحبه وموالاته حتى أن المرأة تهيئ أسباب السفر لزوجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿruf is what God obliges or recommends people to do by reason or revealed law.
rows.anchor: وهو ما أوجب الله فعله أو رغب فيه عقلا أو شرعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munkar is what God forbids or discourages by reason or revealed law.
rows.anchor: وهو ما نهى الله عن فعله وزهد فيه عقلا أو شرعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They persist in prayer, pay zakat from their wealth, direct it where God ordered, and obey and follow the will and approval of God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: يداومون على فعل الصلاة وإخراج الزكاة من أموالهم ووضعها حيث أمر الله تعالى بوضعها فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will have mercy on such believers in the afterlife; He is mighty and wise, able to give mercy or punishment and to place each appropriately.
rows.anchor: أي الذين هذه صفتهم يرحمهم الله في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that enjoining right and forbidding wrong are individual obligations, since it attributes them to all believers without restricting them to a particular group.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر من فروض الأعيان لأنه جعلهما من صفات جميع المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivers flow beneath the trees of Paradise; its dwellings are pleasant and free of harm, illness, and fatigue, according to al-Hasan.
rows.anchor: أي من تحت أشجارها الأنهار والماء فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes Jannat ʿAdn as gardens of permanent residence and eternity.
rows.anchor: أي في جنات إقامة وخلد

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud identifies ʿAdn as the inner center of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي بطنان الجنة أي وسطها عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says ʿAdn is a city in Paradise inhabited by prophets, messengers, martyrs, and guides, with people and gardens surrounding it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي مدينة في الجنة وفيها الرسل والأنبياء والشهداء وأئمة الهدى والناس حولهم والجنان حولها عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi describe ʿAdn as Paradise's highest rank, with the spring Tasnim and surrounding gardens; it has been covered since creation, contains jewel and gold palaces, and receives fragrant white musk from beneath the Throne.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن عدنا أعلى درجة في الجنة وفيها عين التسنيم والجنان حولها محدقة بها وهي مغطاة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The excerpt begins a Prophetic report about the verse but gives no report content before it ends.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making a covenant by saying “I owe God a promise to do this” binds the speaker, since God has legislated and determined the obligation.
rows.anchor: هي أن تقول علي عهد الله لأفعلن كذا فإنه يكون بذلك قد عقد على نفسه وجوب ما ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bukhil originally means refusing a petitioner because giving feels difficult; religious usage applies it to withholding an obligation such as zakat.
rows.anchor: والبخل منع السائل لشدة الإعطاء ثم صار في الشرع لمنع الواجب لأن من منع الزكاة فهو بخيل

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani rejects defining stinginess as withholding an obligation because giving is difficult: then generosity would mean discharging an obligation without difficulty, making a person who pays a debt generous.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني لا يجوز أن يكون البخل منع الواجب لمشقة الإعطاء

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr's poem calls the miser blameworthy wherever he may be and the generous person praiseworthy despite circumstances.
rows.anchor:
كما قال زهير:
إن البخيل ملوم حيث كان ول

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani defines stinginess as withholding what causes no harm if given and no benefit if retained when wisdom calls for giving; the refusal reflects tightness of spirit even without material harm.
rows.anchor: ومن منع ما لا يضره بذله ولا ينفعه منعه مما تدعو إليه الحكمة فهو بخيل لأنه لا يقع المنع على هذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿqaba, awratha, and adda are near-synonyms for succession, bequeathing, and conveying; aʿqaba can also mean requiting, as in al-Nabigha's poem.
rows.anchor: وأعقبه وأورثه وأداه نظاير وقد يكون أعقبه بمعنى جازاه قال النابغة: فمن أطاع فأعقبه بطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najwa is secret speech; its related verbs include nājā, tanājā, and intajā, and its plural is anjiya. The root suggests distance from others, or alternatively a raised place beyond a flood's reach where speech is private.
rows.anchor: والنجوى الكلام الخفي. يقال: ناجيته وتناجوا وانتجوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lamma is like idha here; unlike future-oriented in and idha, lamma and lawla concern what has passed, with lamma indicating that the second event occurred because the first did.
rows.anchor: معنى لما معنى إذا لأن لما الغالب عليها الجزاء وهي اسم يقع في جواب متى يقال متى كان كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second object of “gave them from His bounty” is omitted; the implied object is what they had requested from His bounty.
rows.anchor: فلما آتاهم من فضله المفعول الثاني محذوف تقديره فلما آتاهم ما تمنوه من فضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form lanassaddaqanna derives from lanatasaddaqanna, with tāʾ assimilated into ṣād.
rows.anchor: لنصدقن أصله لنتصدقن أدغمت التاء في الصاد
